To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

“Ancient and modern hybridisation and mitochondrial introgression were found in a group of closely related allopatric monogeneans (Gyrodactylus) parasitising the Eurasian minow Phoxinus phaxinus (L.) in Eurasia.

“The phylogenetic analyses of Gyrodacty-lus species from P. phoxinus in the Eurasian basins of the Black Sea and the Baltic Sea revealed incongruences in the nuclear and mitochondrial phylogeny, suggesting ancient and postglacial hybridisations and mitochondrial introgression.
ancient and modern genome shufflings were detected in four allopatric related species of Gyrodacylus von Nordmann, ectoparasites of the Eurasian minnnow Phoxinusphoxinus (Cypriniformes: Cyprinidae).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ancient and recent reticulate evolution of Gyrodactyla von Nordmann, with the hybridisation of the allopatric species and with the shuffling of the mitochondrial and nuclear genomes.

the phylogeographic and evolutionary processes that have shaped the diversity and distribution of Gyrodactyus on P. phoxinus, including ancient and recent introgression and hybridisation, as well as postglacial dispersals.
a model of ancient hybridisation and subsequent introgression of mtDNA, followed by the postglacial hybridisations, and with the phylogenetic incongruence of the mitochondrial and nuclear genomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
G. pannomicus, G. albolactustris n. s., G. danastriae and G. botniacus n. s. are four closely related allopatric alloparasitic monogenetic species.

G. pannomicus is a species complex, and G. albolacaustrius n. sp., G. botnicu s n. sp. and G. danastriae are its sister taxa, but the phylogenetic relationships of the latter three species are unresolved.
the four species are not monophyletic, but the two species pairs G. pannonus-G. danastriae and G. albolactustris-G. botnicus are monophyletic.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ancient hybridisation has been followed by the postglacial introgression, but both processes were incomplete.
the mitochondrial phylogeny is more reliable for reconstructing the evolutionary history of species than the nuclear phylogeny.
the hybridisation and the introgression of mtDNA have been the driving forces of the evolution of Gyrodactyli in Eurasia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mitochondrial phylogeny can reveal the ancient hybridisation and the nuclear ITS phylogeny can be useful in distinguishing the hybrids from the parental lineages.
the mitochondrial phylogeny is a poor proxy for the nuclear phylogeny, especially for the recent and ancient hybridisations.

the ancient introgression of mtDNA can be detected by the phylogenetic incongruence of the nuclear and mitochondrial genes, and that the hybridisation can be detected even when the hybridisation event is ancient and the species have diverged by more than 1.3 My.
